newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-RONALDO SALARY DOUBLED IN NEW BARCELONA DEAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RONALDO SALARY DOUBLED IN NEW BARCELONA DEAL.

text.p: Barcelona have doubled Ronaldo's annual salary to 500 million pesetas ($3.85 million) in a new deal which will keep the young striker at the club until 2006, according to unofficial reports.

Any team wanting to sign the Brazilian are also likely to have to pay the club 10 billion pesetas ($76.9 million) for his signature. Ronaldo was bought from PSV Eindhoven in the close season for 2.5 billion ($19.23 million), but has already been the subject of several bids after a spectacular start to the Spanish season.
"The business is closed," said Barcelona vice-president Joan Gaspart, who refused to discuss the terms of the deal.

The news comes in the wake of Barcelona's 2-0 defeat at arch-rivals Real Madrid -- in which Ronaldo missed a simple chance -- and follows the Catalan club's tradition of supporting players and managers after set-backs.
Despite a quiet spell in the past few games, Ronaldo still leads the Spanish scoring tables with 13 goals, level with Real's Davor Suker.
